preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `native_godot_project` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

Keep frozen technical baseline `host_godot_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Make the four ordinary enemies semantically and visually distinct, restore a fully navigable and independently adjustable pause/settings flow, and complete authoritative live-HUD, Credits, and victory/failure Result presentation while preserving the verified wave, boss, cemetery, lifecycle and Godot boot baselines.

diagnosis.root_cause: The candidate centralizes distinct product states behind generic presenters: every ordinary enemy instances the same hostile-lantern scene and simulates motion through pivot rotation, bobbing, glow and scale; RunShellView treats nonterminal page navigation like a latched terminal action, groups unrelated settings behind shared controls, and lays information pages out with fixed rectangles; the result path has partial fields in source but lacks a closure-ready terminal snapshot and complete weapon-plus-upgrade presentation proven in both outcomes.

stop_conditions: Stop scope after the five host-selected active issues and three required gaps are closure-ready; do not treat deferred animation, audio, cemetery, camera, lifecycle, performance, upgrade or VFX issues in this iteration.
Do not accept whole-model rotation, bobbing, tinting, scaling or translation as enemy animation, or a shared ordinary-enemy package differentiated only by those operations.

Do not accept Settings if page navigation advances gameplay, leaves action_latched set, loses keyboard/mouse/gamepad focus, changes more than one independent setting per activation, or fails persistence after restart.

Do not accept information presentation if Credits overlap at any supported scale, if live HUD values disagree with the authoritative snapshot, or if either Result outcome omits damage dealt, damage taken, weapon ranks, selected upgrades or working Retry/Title actions.

Stop and retain the current accepted package if a proposed visible asset requires destructive source surgery, breaks its authored rig/material hierarchy, or cannot import and bind cleanly; Developer may replace only the intact provisional ordinary-enemy package.

Keep native_godot_project and host_godot_boot passing, and preserve the authoritative five-wave resource, deterministic cap reconciliation, Bellkeeper package and lifecycle, intact cemetery package, Montserrat shell hierarchy, and restored 100% UI-scale baseline.

strategy.rationale: Change the ownership boundaries that caused the failures instead of applying another transform or spacing pass: give each ordinary role a profile-selected intact presenter with explicit semantic state binding; distinguish nonterminal shell navigation from terminal actions; expose one persisted setting per control and consumer; and commit one immutable terminal run snapshot that drives a structured Result page. This also makes each defect directly retestable through state receipts and representative runtime views.

code: Parse all changed GDScript and load every changed scene/resource without errors; keep project.godot, native_godot_project and host_godot_boot valid.

Inspect resolved ordinary-enemy scene bindings and assert all four role_ids have nonempty, distinct presentation descriptors plus explicit spawn, approach, telegraph, attack, hurt and death semantics.
Exercise pooled enemy reset and cap reconciliation in focused checks: no stale clip/state after reuse, no movement after death, and cap retirement adds zero defeats or rewards.

Exercise shell state transitions as a table: title→settings→title, active→pause→settings→pause→resume, pause→retry, pause→title and pause→quit; assert pause ownership, focus, latch and exactly-one action behavior at every step where applicable only if OS/editor permits quit checks safely without exiting the validation harness. Verify each settings action changes one persisted key and reloads the同?
runtime: GameLoop Runtime/Tester recaptures four separated ordinary-enemy lifecycle sequences from the shipped camera: spawn/approach, telegraph, impact/recovery, hurt/death, with runtime state identifying role, variant, semantic state, velocity and generation; then recaptures one representative 25–40-enemy Wave 4 view.

GameLoop Runtime/Tester verifies Pause Settings with keyboard, mouse and gamepad: gameplay time remains frozen, Back restores Pause, and Resume, Restart, Title and Quit remain usable after navigation.

GameLoop Runtime/Tester changes every setting independently, reconstructs the shell or restarts the run, confirms persistence and runtime effect/target behavior, then restores windowed mode and 100% UI scale.

GameLoop Runtime/Tester captures live HUD during ordinary play and boss play and compares every visible value with the same-frame authoritative snapshot; central movement and attack lanes must remain readable. Developer only prepares candidate state/instrumentation; host and Tester own capture and verdict evidence.
visual: Compare enemy and dense-wave captures with the bound gameplay reference for high-angle silhouette separation, coherent chunky stylization, moonlit cool/warm hierarchy, clear escape lanes and restrained telegraph overlap; do not require its exact layout or trade dress.

Inspect each selected enemy package's actual runtime geometry, materials, textures, alpha mode, pivots, scale and semantic motion. Reject unbound files, matte/chroma edge contamination, broken materials, incompatible style or variants that differ only by palette, mirror, crop, scale or offset.

Capture Settings and Pause at native 1280×720, fullscreen, windowed and supported 90%, 100% and 125% UI scales using the shipped viewport; inspect focus states, text wrapping, control clipping and full-viewport composition.

Capture Credits at native, fullscreen/windowed and supported scales with the final provenance line and Back control simultaneously visible and separated; reject any text/control or focus-outline overlap.

done_when: Mossling, Wispbat, Bone Slinger and Grave Brute each bind a distinct, coherent stylized actor presentation selected by role_id; no two roles resolve to the current single shared ordinary-enemy package, and each remains recognizable by silhouette and motion without relying on tint, scale or mirror-only differences.

Every role exposes spawn, approach driven by actual planar velocity, attack telegraph, attack/damage frame, hurt and death motion through explicit semantic bindings. Gameplay damage aligns with the attack impact, death cannot resume living motion, and pool return resets presentation state before reuse.

Existing combat behavior remains authoritative: melee, flank, ranged lane and slam cues stay distinct; collision, spawn safety, drops, exactly-once defeat rewards and deterministic cap reconciliation are unchanged.

Enemy runtime state exposes role_id, resolved presentation/variant id, semantic state, active clip or authored motion id, velocity and generation so Tester can associate captured motion with authoritative lifecycle events.

At representative Wave 4 density, all four roles and hostile telegraphs remain readable from the shipped high-angle camera, with no broken materials, floating pivots, visible proxies or effects that erase escape lanes.

Visible-family plan is satisfied for family_id enemy.mossling, enemy.wispbat, enemy.bone_slinger and enemy.grave_brute: prd_style_match is cohesive chunky stylized low-poly/cartoon cemetery actors; source_quality_class is intact production-ready rigged or equivalently authored animated packages; material_and_texture_evidence includes runtime-bound material slots, native texture/alpha inspection, ！
tasks.instructions: Replace the single hardwired ordinary-enemy presentation with a role-keyed presenter contract owned by EnemyProfile/EnemyActor. Developer owns bounded asset/reference discovery and must preview candidates under the real camera and moonlight before provisional binding; do not preselect or surgically modify a source package. Preserve gameplay state, pooling and attack causality while mapping those states to authored semantic motion. For each of the four family_ids, expected_runtime_uses_or_visible_area_share is a medium/high-frequency share of the 25–40-enemy peak; minimum_distinct_source_variants and minimum_runtime_variants are 3 per role where exposure is 16–63 and 4 per role if measured exposure reaches 64+, maximum_single_variant_share is 0.40, diversity_axes are meaningful silhouette/gear/material-detail and authored motion variation, background_mode is opaque 3D materials with native transparency only for genuine cutouts, and runtime_evidence_views are separated normal-camera lifecycle sequences for each role plus a representative Wave 4 crowd view. Deterministically select variants from stable_id and spawn generation; palette, mirror, scale, crop and offset aliases do not count as distinct variants.
tasks.title: Give every ordinary enemy a role-owned semantic presenter

done_when: Activating Settings from Pause changes the shell to Settings while get_tree().paused remains true, clears or avoids the terminal action latch, establishes valid focus, and Back returns to the still-usable Pause page.

Resume, Restart Run, Return to Title and Quit remain independently usable after entering and leaving Pause Settings; keyboard, mouse and gamepad activation each produce exactly one authoritative action.

Master volume, music volume, effects volume, window mode, UI scale, screen shake, hit flash, damage numbers, danger contrast and target bias each have a separate focused control with a truthful current value; one activation changes only that control.

Every setting persists independently across shell reconstruction and run restart. Settings with runtime consumers update those consumers without requiring a new run, and target-bias behavior resolves through the authoritative target selector rather than display-only text.
Settings remains fully visible and focusable in native, fullscreen and windowed modes at every supported UI scale; returning the persisted baseline to 100% restores the verified shell composition.
Shell state instrumentation reports mode, return_mode, pause ownership, action_latched, focus path and all individual setting values so Tester can directly verify navigation and mutation isolation.
tasks.instructions: Separate page navigation from terminal shell actions. Add an explicit Settings branch to the run controller, retain the paused resume state across nested navigation, and reserve action_latched for transitions that genuinely commit or leave the page. Replace grouped Display/Accessibility mutations with one control/action per persisted field, with stable focus order and Back semantics. Bind settings to existing semantic consumers where present and keep values truthful when a consumer is unavailable; do not represent several effects as one toggle. Preserve the accepted Montserrat typography, icon controls, full-viewport shell and 100% baseline.
tasks.title: Restore pause navigation and independent accessibility settings

done_when: A terminal result snapshot is committed exactly once before terminal teardown and remains immutable while Result is displayed; both failure and Bellkeeper victory use that snapshot rather than a later mutable live state.

Both Result outcomes visibly show outcome, elapsed time, wave, level, defeated enemies, damage dealt, damage taken, equipped weapon identities and ranks, and selected upgrade/build details, with truthful empty-build wording when applicable.
Retry starts a clean new run and Return to Title performs terminal cleanup from both victory and failure Result pages; focus and action debouncing remain correct for keyboard, mouse and gamepad.

The live HUD continues to bind health, experience, level, wave/run progress, equipped weapons and ranks, dash readiness and contextual boss health from the authoritative RunSnapshot without covering the central arena.

Credits body copy and provenance remain legible and end above a distinct Back control at native, fullscreen and windowed presentation across every supported UI scale; no glyph, icon or focus rectangle overlaps another control.

Result, Credits and live HUD remain compact and authored in the Mournlight lantern/brass/moon-silver language, with no clipped text, debug-like pile, fixed top-left composition or large opaque panel obscuring gameplay.
Runtime state exposes the committed result snapshot and displayed field values so Tester can compare every visible statistic and build item against authoritative state.
tasks.instructions: Complete the run-information pipeline instead of only changing labels. Introduce or retain a single authoritative RunSnapshot schema for live HUD fields, then freeze a terminal copy before failure/victory cleanup and render Result from structured statistics, weapon ranks and selected upgrades. Give Result and Credits page-specific responsive layout constraints so body content and controls cannot share rectangles as viewport or UI scale changes. Preserve Retry/Title behavior, the accepted HUD visual family and the existing provenance content.
tasks.title: Commit truthful run summaries and responsive information pages
